## About these materials

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Citation statement
Please cite these materials as: Von Grebmer zu Wolfsthurn, S., Middleton, S., Ihle, M., & Schönbrodt, F. (2026). *Teaching open research: Core didactic principles* [Quarto slides]. [LMU Open Science Center](https://www.osc.lmu.de/). [https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/core-didactic-principles/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/core-didactic-principles/)
:::

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to **provide future open research instructors and train-the-trainers** with core **teaching skills** to **deliver** Open Research workshops, seminars, lectures and courses etc. through a balanced mix of **theoretical elements** and **hands-on exercises** . Whether you are new to teaching or looking to sharpen your approach, this workshop will give you **theoretical and practical foundations** for designing engaging and effective teaching events focused on bringing Open Research closer to your learners.

### Who are these materials for?

- **Aspiring open research instructors**
- **Future open research train-the-trainers** and **educators** in higher education (e.g., universities, colleges) and
- **Self-learners** 

with familiarity about open research challenges, issues and tools.

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Where to find this  |
|------------|------------|------------|
| Familiarity with Open Research practices | Examples: R, Quarto, Git, GitHub, preregistration, Open Access etc.| [Click here to get familiar with Open Research first](https://lmu-osc.github.io/training/self-learning.html) |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you will ...

- **Remember** basic didactic concepts as the foundation for learning success
- **Explain** and **compare** how knowledge can be organized depending on the level of expertise
- **Evaluate** the alignment between learning objectives, assessment types and teaching activities
- **Formulate** concrete learning objectives according to specific learning domains for real-world content
